title: Card renders bd show --json fields into regions
description: Source.show returns structured detail instead of text: {title, description, acceptance, design, notes, comments, closeReason, children[], waitsOn[], blocks[]}. Beads impl: bd show --json --include-comments --include-dependents. Card: h3 title + id chip; breadcrumb to house; state chips (priority, trade, status, assignee, updated-ago, labels); description first paragraph always shown, rest under more; Done when (acceptance) open by default; design/notes/comments/children collapsed with counts in the summary; children and waitsOn as clickable rows (id, title, priority, age). Empty field = no region. No parsing of bd show text. Keep by-hand actions as is.
acceptance_criteria: Card has no <pre> for beads. First two lines + chips answer act-or-not. Collapsed sections remember open state like by-hand. Tests cover region mapping and empty fields.
notes: Graceful fallback for beads not written to the contract: glance line = first paragraph if there is a blank line, else first sentence (split on '. ' or newline), else first ~140ch at a word boundary with an ellipsis; the rest goes under more. Missing acceptance/design/notes = no region, no empty heading. Description that is one long paragraph still gets 60ch wrapping and markdown-lite. Never show a 'not to contract' warning on the card.

dependencies.title: Card reads like a glance, not a wall
dependencies.description: Bead detail is bd show text in one <pre>: ~90ch lines, 1.0 leading, caps labels, status inferred from dates, tip footer. Reading norms (F-pattern, inverted pyramid, chunking, 45-75ch, progressive disclosure, recognition over recall) say: state as chips, relationships as links, prose last and narrow. Glance/detail split is authored by the agent at creation (title / description first line / acceptance / design / notes), not parsed at render. Card renders bd show --json fields into regions; site adds the one dynamic line (why it is on screen: age, blocker fan-out).
dependencies.acceptance_criteria: Card answers 'do I act, on what' in two lines without reading prose. No bd show text parsing. Prime tells agents the writing contract. Doctor reports compliance.
dependencies.notes: Existing beads and specs were not written to the contract and most never will be. Card must read well from any bead: contract is a bonus, not a requirement. Nothing nags inside the card.
